memos.scout:
Case for buying Ouroboros now:

The strongest signal is breadth of demand. The last 15 minutes show 265 distinct buyers against 264 sellers, but buy SOL of 202 versus sell SOL of 174, a positive net flow of 28 SOL, and an 87% return over the window. Only 13.5% of buy volume came from the top 3 holders, and the first two minutes after graduation had 302 buyers with a top-5 buyer share of 13%. The curve shows 226 buyers with a 44% completer share, meaning many participants completed the bonding curve rather than a few whales.

The coin is only 9.5% off its 30-minute high, with no airdrop dump seen and a classification of ORGANIC, which the base rates treat better than factory coins.

Caveats: bundling at 28% of the curve and a launch bot present, sell-to-buy near 1.07 right after graduation, and a pool of only 88 SOL mean round-trip costs of several percent and real exit risk. Base rates still say most coins lose from here. The case is thin but not empty; I'd call it a marginal, not a strong, buy.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: distribution into the 0.87x run-up. In the last 15 minutes, sellers (264) nearly matched buyers (265), and sell SOL (173.8) was 86% of buy SOL (202.0), so net flow was only +28 SOL against a stock that already ran hard. The 30-minute high sits only 9.5% above price, so this is a fading peak, not a fresh breakout. A 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost on a $20 ticket, with only 87.8 SOL of pool depth, means a retrace of 10% or more is needed just to break even, and a single large holder exit could take a bigger bite. The launch bot in the first two minutes and a 27.8% bundle share mean early supply was concentrated. Skip.
